subject: Pace stress test trigger — proposed MAP reset and contingency
messages:
From: Martin Cole <mcole@nimblehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick: evaluation pace stress test flagged — can we talk?

Ava,

Thanks for the call yesterday. We ran the internal readiness checkpoint with security and procurement this morning and flagged two items that are going to slow the evaluation: additional SOC evidence requests and a procurement queue for vendor onboarding. Both are likely to push our demo/eval window by at least 2 weeks unless we compress other tasks.

Can you share the MAP and a suggested contingency so we can present to our CTO tomorrow? Procurement asked for a single-sheet timeline that shows what slips and what stays.

Appreciate a rapid response — Martin
Martin Cole
Head of Platform Engineering, NimbleHealth
[Attachment: procurement-questions-20261130.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Martin Cole <mcole@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: evaluation pace stress test flagged — can we talk?

Martin —

Thanks for the heads up. I pulled the current MAP and the last eval schedule (attached). High level proposal: run a 10-day "pace stress test" that condenses the non-dependent activities (integration smoke + data ingestion) into parallel lanes, and hold a reduced-scope feature demo that verifies SLAs and latency. If procurement needs the vendor onboarding completed first, we can flip the order and run the demo with masked data + contract stub.

I'll outline a single-sheet contingency and a small risk log below for your CTO briefing. If that looks OK we can follow with an updated MAP PDF and a one-time credit for expanded support during the stress window.

Proposed single-sheet summary (short):
- New provisional close window: original 2027-01-14 -> provisional 2027-01-28 (14-day buffer)
- Stress test window: 2026-12-07 -> 2026-12-17 (10 days) focusing on ingest + baseline latency
- Must-have deliverables during stress test: integration runbook, perf smoke, SOC evidence baseline packet
- Contingency triggers: any procurement hold > 72h triggers demo-with-masked-data flow

Quick risk log (high-level):
1) Procurement queue (High) — impact: eval delay; mitigation: prioritized contract template + dedicated SE support to answer onboarding checklist within 24-48h.
2) SOC evidence request (Medium-High) — impact: stalls security sign-off; mitigation: deliver partial evidence set + SOC-2 control mapping; schedule audit evidence drop on day 6 of stress test.
3) Data access latency (Medium) — impact: longer ingest time; mitigation: use sample batched dataset and parallelize ingestion lanes.

Attaching MAP_v1.3.pdf and a condensed schedule.

Ava Chen
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MAP_v1.3.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Martin Cole <mcole@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: evaluation pace stress test flagged — can we talk?

Looping in technical action items and my availability. Ava — I can own the perf smoke validation and the KV/prefix cache verification during the stress window. Recommended adjustments to MAP:
- Move "full dataset soak" to parallel lane and reduce required ingest size from 5M tokens to 500k for the initial perf pass.
- Drop non-essential function calls for the demo (keep generation + embeddings path only).
- Add one fallback model (lower-quant) for latency-critical tests.

I'll prepare the runbook and the checklist for procurement so they can mark items as complete. If Nimble wants a Friday checkpoint call, I can do 12/11.

--Priyom
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Nimble_Eval_Schedule_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Martin Cole <mcole@nimblehealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: evaluation pace stress test flagged — can we talk?

Ava / Priyom —

This is helpful. Our CTO reviewed the single-sheet and asked us to proceed with the pace stress test starting 12/07. Procurement will continue their vendor onboarding in parallel but confirmed they can mark items as "in progress" to keep our window open.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood sign a limited-scope non-prod data handling addendum (we'll share a template) so procurement moves faster?
- If the stress test identifies a regression, can Redwood provide a 5-day remediation SLA to keep us inside the provisional 1/28 ship window?

I'll upload the procurement template by EOD.

Martin

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Martin Cole <mcole@nimblehealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: evaluation pace stress test flagged — can we talk?

Martin —

Thanks — confirmed. We accept the pace stress test start 2026-12-07 and will deliver the condensed MAP update by EOD 12/01 (attached drive link). On your two asks:

1) Non-prod addendum: Redwood legal will review your template on receipt; we will prioritize a short turn review and flag any blocking terms within 48 hours.
2) 5-day remediation SLA for stress-test blockers: Redwood can offer a targeted remediation SLA for any functional regressions discovered during the stress window, limited to items impacting the agreed must-have deliverables. We will document the scope in the MAP update and include an exec-level escalation path (Laura Bennett to own).

Updated risk register (post-discussion):
- Procurement queue: Residual risk reduced to Medium if procurement marks items in progress. Owner: NimbleHealth procurement / Redwood SEs.
- SOC evidence: Owner: Redwood compliance. Deliverable schedule: partial packet day 4, full baseline day 10.
- Remediation capacity: Owner: Redwood engineering; SLA: 5 business days for qualifying regressions.
- Contingency: If remediation exceeds SLA, provisional close moves to 2027-02-04 (14 additional days) unless execs approve exception.

Next steps:
- Martin: send procurement addendum template (procurement@nimblehealth.com)
- Priyom: share perf runbook + checklist by 12/03
- Laura: I will send the exec escalation note and updated MAP PDF by 12/01 17:00 PT.

Ava Chen
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwoodinference.com
